# warpbuild_runner_image (Resource)

A BYOC (bring-your-own-cloud) AWS AMI runner image. The image's OS, architecture and root device are derived from the AMI by WarpBuild. Updating `ami_id` creates a new image version in place; older versions are purged automatically.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "warpbuild_stack" "ec2" {
  alias = "my-ec2-stack"
}

resource "warpbuild_runner_image" "custom" {
  alias    = "my-custom-image"
  stack_id = data.warpbuild_stack.ec2.id
  ami_id   = "ami-0123456789abcdef0"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `alias` (String) Name of the image. Unique within the organization and immutable.
- `ami_id` (String) AWS AMI ID of the customer-owned image. Changing this creates a new image version in place.
- `stack_id` (String) ID of the EC2 stack the image belongs to. Use the `warpbuild_stack` data source to look this up.

### Read-Only

- `arch` (String) CPU architecture, derived from the AMI.
- `id` (String) Runner image ID.
- `os` (String) Operating system, derived from the AMI.
- `purge_image_versions_offset` (Number) Number of image versions kept before older ones are purged. Managed by WarpBuild.
- `status` (String) Image status.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import warpbuild_runner_image.custom <runner-image-id>
```
